title.t: The ruleset does not cover this kind of content

when.t: The signed ruleset lists the content types it covers, and the content under review is another type.

steps.t: Agent 17 flags it as uncovered; it is never approved by omission.
The type comes from the submitter, or from which agent sent it (Agent 12 sends advertising).
A ruleset that does not list the types it covers flags nothing as uncovered.

never.t: Approve content the ruleset does not address.

you_see.t: A flagged verdict, passed to the authorized user by the submitting agent.

test.t: The ruleset covers listing descriptions, nurture sequences, buyer criteria, client messages and social replies, not advertising. A signed ad "Open house Sunday, bright kitchen" is reviewed.

when.t: Content that was flagged is submitted again unchanged.

steps.t: Agent 17 checks it again in full and raises a legal-line alert that it was resubmitted unchanged.
The verdict follows the fresh check.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert about the repeat, and the flagged verdict.

test.t: The ad "Perfect for young families near the park" is submitted twice.

when.t: A review has waited more than 1 day on a daily run (the tuning default).

steps.t: Agent 17 tells the authorized user the review is overdue, naming the submitting agent and whether a ruleset is active. It does not rush a verdict.
A review only waits when no ruleset is loaded. The clock starts on the first daily run that sees it, because submitters send no date.
The overdue note is sent once for each waiting review (fixed 2026-10-28; it used to repeat on every daily run).

never.t: Rush a verdict to meet a deadline.

you_see.t: A note that the review is overdue and no ruleset is active.

test.t: No ruleset is loaded. A listing description goes to review; daily runs on October 15 and 17.

title.t: A state rule is stricter than the federal rules

when.t: Content for a state matches one of that state's phrases in the ruleset.

steps.t: Agent 17 flags it, naming the phrase, the rule and the state.
The state travels with the content from the submitter.
Agent 17 applies only the ruleset the authorized user signs: listed phrases, optional state phrases, and optionally the content types and states it covers. It matches exact phrases.

never.t: Pass content because it meets the federal rules only.

you_see.t: A flagged verdict naming the Ohio rule.

test.t: The ruleset has an Ohio rule against "exclusive community"; an Ohio ad says "An exclusive community near the park".

title.t: Someone asks to pre-approve a kind of content

when.t: The authorized user's signed setting asks Agent 17 to pre-approve a class of templates.

steps.t: Agent 17 refuses and stores nothing: every piece of content gets its own review.

you_see.t: A note that pre-approval was refused.

test.t: A request to pre-approve "all open house invitations".

when.t: Content contains a phrase the ruleset prohibits.

steps.t: Agent 17 flags it, citing the exact phrase and rule. There is no approve-with-a-note.
Only the exact listed phrases are caught.
Agent 17 applies only the ruleset the authorized user signs: listed phrases, optional state phrases, and optionally the content types and states it covers. It matches exact phrases.

never.t: Approve steering language with a note.

you_see.t: A flagged verdict citing "perfect for young families" (FH-1).

test.t: An ad "A quiet street, perfect for young families".

title.t: An ad lacks the brokerage identification

when.t: Advertising under review does not contain the brokerage identification the authorized user signed, or none is signed.

steps.t: Agent 17 flags it; there is no exception for short formats.
Agent 17 checks against its own signed setting, not what the submitter says.

never.t: Approve an ad without the brokerage identification.

you_see.t: A flagged verdict: brokerage identification missing.

test.t: Agent 12 has no brokerage identification; an ad "Open house Sunday, bright kitchen" is reviewed.

when.t: Content Agent 17 has seen before comes back.

steps.t: Agent 17 checks it fresh against the ruleset in force, not from its earlier verdict.
If the earlier verdict was flagged, the repeat alert (17-02) is raised as well, even when the copy now passes.

never.t: Repeat an earlier verdict without checking.

you_see.t: A new verdict under the current ruleset.

test.t: "Perfect for young families near the park" is flagged under ruleset r1; r2, without that phrase, is signed; the same copy is approved.

title.t: A state's rules have not been reviewed by counsel

when.t: The ruleset lists the states counsel has reviewed, and the content is for another state or names none.

steps.t: Agent 17 flags it and raises a legal-line alert for counsel.
A ruleset that lists no reviewed states raises nothing here.

never.t: Clear content on general knowledge of a state's rules.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert naming the state.

test.t: Counsel has reviewed Ohio only; a Pennsylvania ad "Bright kitchen" is reviewed.

title.t: One agent keeps sending near-miss language

when.t: Agent 17 flags content from the same agent for the third time.

steps.t: Agent 17 sends the authorized user a report naming the agent and the count, then starts counting again.

test.t: Three ads from Agent 12 with prohibited phrases.
